profile.reading:
This OSM record, "Tahoe Reno 4," is mapped to Switch's "Citadel Campus" in the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center, Storey County, Nevada, sharing the same 1 Superloop Circle address as the other numbered Tahoe Reno buildings in this dataset, but could not be confirmed as an individually named or specified Switch facility this session. Switch's own website, full press-release archive, and its FY2021 SEC 10-K filing, its last as a public company before the 2022 DigitalBridge/IFM take-private transaction, name and give specifications only for Tahoe Reno 1 (opened, 1.3 million-plus square feet, 130 megawatts) and, at a groundbreaking stage with no individual specs, Tahoe Reno 2 and 3; no Switch press release, SEC filing, or campus page found this session names a "Tahoe Reno 4" specifically. The FY2021 10-K discloses seven future facilities in aggregate (5.89 million square feet, 520 megawatts combined) without individually naming or numbering them, which likely explains why third-party mapping data assigns sequential "Tahoe Reno 4" and "Tahoe Reno 5" labels, since these appear to be placeholder or extrapolated labels applied by mapping or aggregator sources rather than confirmed Switch-published building names. This profile does not assert that a building called "Tahoe Reno 4" specifically exists as a distinct, confirmed structure separate from the campus's undifferentiated future-facility total, consistent with this dataset's practice of flagging genuine ambiguity rather than guessing. Switch's current marketing describes the full Citadel Campus at up to 17.4 million square feet and more than 2 gigawatts of power at completion.

Storey County's Tahoe Reno Industrial Center spans roughly 107,000 acres and hosts more than 100 tenants beyond Switch, including Tesla's Gigafactory and Google, drawing more than 900 megawatts of on-site power generation capacity across the broader industrial park. Nevada's data center tax abatement program under NRS 360.754 offers a 10-year abatement for a minimum 25 million dollar investment and 10 Nevada jobs, or a 20-year abatement for a minimum 100 million dollar investment and 50 jobs, both requiring pay at or above the statewide average wage; while this program plausibly applies to Switch's continued Citadel Campus buildout in general, no source found this session ties it to a specifically confirmed "Tahoe Reno 4" building.

reading.body:
Switch's Tahoe Reno 4 facility is one of five buildings currently tracked at the Citadel Campus, a 2,000 acre site in Storey County designed for up to 650 MW at full buildout, but this registry does not assign megawatts to individual buildings within it.

The Citadel Campus sits adjacent to Tesla's Gigafactory in an industrial zone optimized for power-intensive operations. Its scale, planned across multiple buildings rather than a single structure, reflects the economics of AI infrastructure: operators consolidate capacity at sites with available grid power and land. Switch's strategy of developing five exascale campuses across different US regions suggests a distribution model, moving compute closer to different power sources rather than concentrating it.

The data does not specify how much of the 650 MW target has been built or energized, nor does it reveal the actual power draw of Tahoe Reno 4 itself. It covers footprint and ambition, not the grid constraint that determines when and whether these buildings actually run at scale.
